target_customer: Newcomers to the US such as international students and workers without an SSN or US credit history
problem: Newcomers cannot get US bank accounts or credit cards without credit history, even if they had strong credit abroad.
business_model: Consumer fintech: debit and credit card interchange and credit building products via partner banks

founders.name: Naveen Qureshi
founders.background_notes: Had strong Canadian credit but could not get a US card after moving to New York.

founders.name: Towers Wilen
founders.background_notes: Met Qureshi in class per Laidlaw announcement; YC page gives no background.

founders.name: Joseph Finlayson
founders.background_notes: Listed as a founder on the YC page with no details.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile banking on a partner bank with card issuing, KYC without SSN and credit reporting is integration heavy but uses existing banking infrastructure.

defensibility.rationale: Relied on partner banks and no proprietary data is evidenced; copyable by other neobanks and credit builders.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copy is documented in sources opened; the company was reportedly sold to Snap Finance per a single anonymous report.

market_need_then: Founder personal experience of being denied credit after moving to the US, and the stated barrier that many issuers require an SSN (Nova Credit guidance).

branding.domain_note: sablecard.com; the site no longer resolves from the research environment.

identity.logo: Logo and 3D card renders appear in designer portfolios on Dribbble; no description sourced.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself. Name is simple but shared with unrelated companies.

outcome_analysis: Sable grew to over 400,000 account holders about a year after full launch, per the July 2022 Laidlaw announcement, which supports real demand among newcomers. It raised only small disclosed money and the YC page lists it as acquired, with a single anonymous report naming Snap Finance. Product Hunt comments mention accounts being closed. The cause of the sale and its date are not public in sources found.
notes: Seedtable lists a 2.7M seed in Feb 2020 and CB Insights lists 3.85M across five rounds; both aggregators, unverified, not recorded. Dealroom lists Y Combinator, JAM Fund, Wheelhouse and others as seed investors, unverified. Acquirer Snap Finance and August 2023 date come from CB Insights and Dealroom citing PitchBook with an anonymous source; unverified so acquirer is null. Website unreachable. No dated competitor source found.
